refuted.claim: Fact #5 (confidence 'verified'): 'the erase/enter behaviour is a property of the CPU's input store cycle and the channel data registers (E-1/E-2, F-1/F-2), described under the device-independent heading Data Transmission, not a per-device quirk. It therefore applies identically to 1402 reader, 729/7330 tape read-with-word-marks, 1011 paper tape and 1415 console in load mode.'
refuted.why: The device-independent 'Data Transmission' section of 223-2692 (printed pp.8-11) never states load-mode word-mark erasure. Its only 'existing word marks' sentence is the MOVE-mode one, and even that sits in a paragraph explicitly about the 1402: 'During move mode data transmission (Figure 6), punched card information from the 1402 reader is encoded into BCD as it is being read into the 1414 buffer, and the information is transferred, unchanged, to core storage. Existing word marks in core storage are retained.' A full-text grep of the extracted manual (1.15 MB of text) finds the phrase 'existing word mark' exactly twice: that move-mode line on printed p.9, and the load-mode line on printed p.58 inside the '1411-1402 Reader Operation' chapter. Figure 5 is likewise a 1402 card example. 223-2692 has no per-device sentence for 729/7330 tape or 1011 paper tape saying existing word marks are removed. The generalization is a sound INFERENCE from the shared E-1/E-2 channel-data-register store path, but it is not what any heading or sentence in the manual states, and the finder labelled it 'verified'.
refuted.correction: Split the claim. VERIFIED: load mode erases existing word marks in the positions it stores, for a 1402 card read (223-2692 p.58 + Figure 5 p.8), and for the 1415 console printer in load mode (A22-0526-3 Figure 44, RCPW: 'WM in storage are erased and entered'). LIKELY (mechanism-based inference, no manual sentence): the same erasure for 729/7330 read-tape-with-word-marks and 1011 paper tape. The mechanism that supports the inference is 223-2692 printed p.11, load-mode input Case 2c: 'The E-1 WM and C-bit lines (no WM is present) are inverted and copied into E-2, producing an odd parity WM character in E-2 that is transferred to 1411 core storage' - i.e. the whole eight-bit character including the WM bit is assembled in the channel register and stored, so nothing of the old core byte survives. That path is shared by every channel device.
refuted.source: IBM 1411 Input-Output Operations, CE Instruction-Reference Manual, Form 223-2692 (1963), printed pp.8-11 ('Data Transmission', 'SEVEN-BIT DEVICES', 'MOVE MODE', 'LOAD MODE', 'LOAD MODE CHARACTER PROCESSING' Cases 1-3) and printed p.58 ('1411-1402 Reader Operation'). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/223-2692_CE_Instruction_1411_Input-Output_Operations_1963.pdf

refuted.claim: Summary paragraph 2: 'Group-mark-with-word-mark: it is neither consumed nor overwritten - it is preserved, and it is never written by a load-mode read.'
refuted.why: The absolute 'never written' is contradicted by the manual's own load-mode assembly rule and by the finder's own open question #3, so the summary is internally inconsistent. 223-2692 printed p.11, Case 2, is unconditional about the character the word mark lands on: 'The BCD portion of the following character is copied from E-1 into E-2 ... producing an odd parity WM character in E-2 that is transferred to 1411 core storage.' If the card image contains a word separator immediately followed by a group-mark character (BCD 77), load mode assembles and stores a genuine GM-WM. The store-gate test on printed p.59 ('If the B-channel is not a GM-WM, input cycle load becomes active') inspects the OLD contents of the target position, not the character being assembled, so nothing blocks the store; the freshly written GM-WM is then sensed on the NEXT cycle and terminates the transfer early with WLR on (A22-0526-3 p.62).
refuted.correction: A load-mode read cannot write a word mark onto a position that already holds a GM-WM, and it never fabricates a GM-WM out of nothing. But it CAN create one at a position it stores, if the card image holds a word separator immediately followed by a group-mark character. An emulated card loader must therefore either guarantee that pattern never occurs in its deck format, or model the resulting early termination. Confidence: likely - the mechanism is documented, the specific case is not called out in any manual I read, and rcornwell/sims implements exactly this (chan_write_char: 'if (cmd[chan] & CHAN_WM && ch != 035) ch |= WM;' with no group-mark exclusion, so ch==077 becomes WM|077).
refuted.source: Form 223-2692 (1963), printed pp.11 (LOAD MODE CHARACTER PROCESSING, Case 2) and 59 (input cycle load gating). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/223-2692_CE_Instruction_1411_Input-Output_Operations_1963.pdf ; rcornwell/sims I7000/i7010_chan.c chan_write_char(). https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c

refuted.claim: Fact #10 attributes the BAR-stepping mechanism to 223-2692 p.42: 'Combined with the extra-E-cycle mechanism (BAR is stepped on the cycle that tests the GM-WM), BAR ends one position PAST the group-mark-word-mark' - sourced to 'mechanism from Form 223-2692 p.42'.
refuted.why: Printed p.42 (and the parallel passage on printed p.59) describes the extra E-cycle and the latches it sets, but says nothing whatever about the B-address register being stepped. The four listed functions of the last-input-cycle latch are: set internal end of transfer, block the end-of-record latch from a wrap-around condition, block the A-channel VC error circuits, and condition the assembly controls to use the B-channel character. No address-register statement appears. The conclusion is correct, but the cited page does not support it.
refuted.correction: The conclusion (final BAR = address(GM-WM) + 1) holds, but cite A22-0526-3 p.99 instead. Its '1401 Compatibility / B-Address Register' chart states that at the completion of a card or print operation BAR differs between the two machines, and gives 1401 op 1 (Read) -> BAR 081 on a 1401 versus 082 on a 1410 running in 1401 mode. Reading 80 columns into 001-080, the 1401 stops at 081 and the 1410 stops at 082: the 1410 takes exactly one extra address step at the end of a card read that the 1401 does not. Same chart is repeated in the CE Handbook 223-2588-2 p.52. That is direct evidence for the extra cycle stepping BAR.
refuted.source: IBM 1410 Principles of Operation, Form A22-0526-3, '1401 Compatibility - B-Address Register' chart, p.99. http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf ; IBM 1410 CE Handbook, Form 223-2588-2 (April 1964), same chart, p.52. http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf

upgraded.claim: 1410: the final B-address register value after a Read a Card is one position PAST the group-mark-word-mark, because the CPU takes an extra address-stepping cycle at the end of the transfer that the 1401 does not take. (Finder asserted the mechanism with a citation that does not contain it; now independently sourced.)
upgraded.source: A22-0526-3 p.99, '1401 Compatibility - B-Address Register': 1401 op 1 (Read) leaves BAR = 081; a 1410 in 1401 mode leaves BAR = 082 (op 4 Punch: 181 vs 183; op 2 Print: 333 vs 335). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf . Corroborated in 223-2588-2 p.52. http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf

additions.claim: 1401-vs-1410 TRAP (the big one for a card loader): on the IBM 1401 the console LOAD KEY does a blanket 80-position word-mark clear - 'The I-address register is set to 001, and a word mark is set in address 001. All other word marks in addresses 002 through 080 are removed.' That is a 1401 console-key behavior, not an op-code behavior, and it has NO 1410 analogue. The 1410's load-mode read clears word marks only in the positions it actually stores, which for a card with word separators is FEWER than 80 - and it sets no word mark in position 1 unless card column 1 is a word separator. Do not implement a 1410 card loader as 'clear WMs across the whole 80-position read-in area'.
additions.source: IBM 1401 Data Processing System Reference Manual, Form A24-1403-5, 'LOAD KEY', printed p.117 ('Operating Keys, Lights, and Switches', 1402 Card Read-Punch). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1401/A24-1403-5_1401_Reference_Apr62.pdf

additions.claim: 1401-vs-1410 TRAP: load-mode word-separator RUN handling differs between the machines. 1401: 'any number (one or more) of word separator characters read in succession from tape are eliminated and a word mark is placed over the first non-word separator character that follows.' 1410: 'a pair of adjacent word separator characters on tape are read into core storage as one word separator character and no word mark is placed over the next non-word separator character.' The 1410 rule is pairwise, the 1401 rule is greedy. The finder's pairwise table row is the 1410 rule and is correct; anyone cross-reading 1401 documentation will get the greedy rule and produce wrong core images.
additions.source: IBM 1410 Customer Engineering Handbook, Form 223-2588-2 (April 1964), '1401/1410 Differences - Read and Write Tape Operations (with word marks)', p.52. http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/223-2588-2_1410_CE_Handbook_196404.pdf

additions.claim: 1410: the mechanical reason load mode replaces the whole target byte. 223-2692 printed p.11, load-mode input Case 2: (a) a WS in E-1 sets a WS into E-2; (b) the BCD portion of the FOLLOWING character is copied from E-1 into E-2; (c) 'The E-1 WM and C-bit lines (no WM is present) are inverted and copied into E-2, producing an odd parity WM character in E-2 that is transferred to 1411 core storage.' Case 1 (no WS) copies 'the same as in move mode', i.e. E-1 BCD, WM and C-bit into E-2 - and a seven-bit device's E-1 WM bit is always 0. So the stored byte's BCD, WM and C bits all come from the channel register; the old core byte contributes nothing. This is the load-mode store rule to implement, and it is stronger evidence than the parity aside in the finder's open question 2.
additions.source: Form 223-2692 (1963), 'LOAD MODE CHARACTER PROCESSING', Input Cases 1-3, printed p.11 (PDF p.15). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/223-2692_CE_Instruction_1411_Input-Output_Operations_1963.pdf

additions.claim: 1410: Read a Card has no escape from GM-WM termination. Its instruction form allows only d-character R (A22-0526-3 p.62). The $ / X d-modifier that suppresses GM-WM termination is a TAPE facility: 'The X d-character may also be used, as described in Read or Write Tape, to prevent any group-mark-word-mark in the program from stopping the data transfer.' So a card read ALWAYS stops at the first GM-WM in the receiving area. rcornwell/sims models this as CHAN_NOREC (set for 'Mod $ or X'), and both of its GM-WM tests are guarded by '(cmd[chan] & CHAN_NOREC) == 0' - a guard the finder's facts #15 and its termination table omit. Harmless for cards, wrong if the same code path is reused for tape.
additions.source: A22-0526-3 p.62 (Read a Card instruction form, d-CHARACTER R) and p.87 (Read/Write Tape with Word Marks). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf ; rcornwell/sims I7000/i7010_chan.c chan_cmd() 'if (dcmd & 0100) cmd[chan] |= CHAN_NOREC;' and chan_write_char(). https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c

additions.claim: 1410: wrong-length record is a status indicator that does not stop the program, but leaving WLR and CLR inconsistent is a hard error at test time: 'The two latches, WLR and CLR, must be in agreement at the end of an I-O operation or a subsequent programmed test of the WLR indicator (BWL) results in a mismatch between the branch latch and the no branch latch. An instruction check occurs during a branch operation if the branch and no branch latches do not match.' An emulator that models WLR must also model CLR as its complement, or programmed BWL tests will misbehave.
additions.source: Form 223-2692 (1963), 'E-CHANNEL WRONG LENGTH RECORD', printed p.42 (PDF p.46). http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/CE_Instruction_Reference_Maintenance/1411_CPU/223-2692_CE_Instruction_1411_Input-Output_Operations_1963.pdf

additions.claim: 1410: Select Stacker and Feed (SSF, op K / 4, d = 0, 1 or 2) leaves BAR = Bp (previous contents, unchanged) and 'Word Marks: Word marks are not affected.' Useful as the negative control when testing a loader that uses the x3=9 read-without-feed form followed by SSF.

1410 vs 1401, 51-column read feed, second trap: in 1401 mode all 80 buffer positions transfer, and positions 1-14 and 66-80 of the 1410's read buffer are 'filled with valid blanks' which are then stored as blanks over core - whereas a real 1401 'leaves the storage locations 1 through 14 and 66 through 80 undisturbed'. PrincOps warns: 'the program must not place data in those locations, or must move it elsewhere in core storage before a card is read.' The finder's fact #13 covered the 1410-mode half (51 active positions, GM-WM in the 52nd position of the read-in area) and is correct; this is the other half.
additions.source: A22-0526-3, '57-Column Cards' [sic - the heading is a typo for 51-Column] under 1401 Compatibility, p.100, body text and footnote. http://www.bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/1410/A22-0526-3_1410_princOps.pdf ; same feature described at p.65 ('a group-mark - word-mark must be inserted in the 52nd position of the core storage read-in area. The 51 active positions, but not the blanks, are transferred').

additions.claim: 223-2692 contradicts itself on which devices are eight-bit, and the finder repeated the correct half. Printed p.8: 'The IBM 1415 Console and the disk storage units (IBM 1301, IBM 1311, and IBM 1405) are eight-bit devices.' Printed p.9, next paragraph: 'All I-O units except the disk storage units are seven-bit devices.' The p.8 version is the one A22-0526-3 supports, since RCPW enters word marks into storage directly from the console. Implement the console as eight-bit.

Partial answer to the finder's open question 5 (1401-compatibility mode word marks): 223-2588-2 p.52 documents 1401-mode differences for tape load mode, stacker select, parity, BAR and the 1402 character set, but states no card-read word-mark difference. It does add one rule the finder did not have: 'When reading in 1401 Mode, if an IRG is encountered before a GMWM is encountered, a GMWM is inserted at that point.' A22-0526-3 pp.99-100 likewise lists no card-read word-mark difference. Absence of a listed difference in two 1401-mode difference lists is weak evidence that the 1410 rule carries into 1401 mode; I did not read 223-2597, so this remains open.

Oracle divergence CONFIRMED and traced end to end. rcornwell/sims chan_cmd() sets 'cmd[chan] |= CHAN_WM; /* Force first char to have word mark set */' in the else branch of the CHAN_LOAD test, i.e. for MOVE mode. Nothing clears CHAN_WM before the first data character. In chan_write_char() (channel -> memory, the input path) the first branch requires (CHAN_LOAD|CHAN_WM)==CHAN_LOAD and so is skipped, and control falls into 'if (cmd[chan] & CHAN_WM && ch != 035) ch |= WM;' - so the first character of a MOVE-mode input record is stored with a word mark. In chan_read_char() (the output path) CHAN_WM is only consulted under CHAN_LOAD, so the flag has no output effect. The divergence is real, input-only, and contradicts 223-2692 p.58 and Figure 5 p.8. Follow the manual.
additions.source: rcornwell/sims, I7000/i7010_chan.c: chan_cmd() (CHAN_WM set for non-L opcode), chan_write_char() (WM forced on first char), chan_read_char() (CHAN_WM gated on CHAN_LOAD). https://github.com/rcornwell/sims/blob/master/I7000/i7010_chan.c

additions.claim: Minor sourcing correction to fact #14: the sims store is not unconditional. The actual code is 'cmd[chan] &= ~CHAN_WM; if ((cmd[chan] & CHAN_LOAD) == 0) ch |= M[caddr[chan]] & WM; if ((chan_flags[chan] & DEV_REOR) == 0) M[caddr[chan]] = ch; caddr[chan]++;'. The finder's quote drops the DEV_REOR guard. The substance (OR-in of the existing WM guarded to move mode; load mode replaces the byte outright) is unaffected, and note that caddr is stepped even when the DEV_REOR guard suppresses the store.

notes:
Verification method: downloaded 223-2692 from bitsavers and extracted with pdftotext -layout (it has a good OCR layer, 1.15 MB of text); rendered printed p.8 (PDF p.12) to PNG at 160 dpi and read the image directly to check Figure 5's annotations and its worked example. A22-0526-3, A22-1407-2, 223-2588-2 and A22-6726 have no usable embedded text layer, so I used the archive.org OCR text already present in the scratchpad for those and cross-checked distinctive strings.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED, verbatim, against the primary source (finder was right, no change): the p.58 move-mode and load-mode prose in full including 'In load mode operation, existing word marks in the input field are removed'; Figure 5's two annotations 'Existing Word Marks In Core Storage Are Not Disturbed' and 'Existing Word Marks Are Erased'; Figure 5's worked example, which the rendered image confirms exactly as the finder described it (card WS,A,WS,B,WS,WS,C -> load-mode core positions 1-4 = A with WM, B with WM, WS with NO WM, C with no WM, positions 5-7 drawn empty; move-mode core = the seven characters one for one); the two-consecutive-word-separators rule and the impossibility of a WM-over-WS from a seven-bit device (p.9); the p.59 store gate 'If the B-channel is not a GM-WM, input cycle load becomes active to gate the input character from E-2 into 1411 core storage (ALD 12.50.01)'; the p.42 extra-E-cycle passage and all four functions of the last-input-cycle latch including item 4 'Conditions the assembly controls to use the B-channel character (to regenerate the character read out on the extra E-cycle)'; A22-0526-3 p.41 'the input record length is shortened one position in either of these operations: storing one word mark, or storing one word separator'; A22-0526-3 p.62 in full (word-separator-to-word-mark rule, 'The operation is stopped by the first group-mark - word-mark sensed in core storage', 'A group-mark - word-mark must appear in the core-storage position to the immediate right of the data record', 'If the [GM-WM] is incorrectly positioned, the wrong-length record channel status indicator will turn on', BAR = B + LB + 1); Figure 8 p.12 'LB - The number of characters in the B-field'; Figure 44 RCP 'WM in storage are undisturbed' / RCPW 'WM in storage are erased and entered'; A22-1407-2's console row; 223-2588-2's I/O Printer row 'L-mode: WMs erased and entered. M-mode: WMs in storage undisturbed'; and the documentation gap itself - I checked A22-0526-3's tape sections (pp.87ff, Figure 98 Word Mark Translation for Tape), its Word Marks introduction (p.10), and its console load read/write section (p.48), and none of them states load-mode erasure. The gap claim stands.

The finder's central conclusion is correct and the sourcing for it is solid. The three refutations above are about overreach and mis-citation, not about the answer: (1) the generalization from cards to tape/paper tape is an inference, not a documented statement - downgrade to likely; (2) 'a GM-WM is never written by a load-mode read' is false as stated and contradicts the finder's own open question 3; (3) the BAR-stepping mechanism is not on 223-2692 p.42 - I found a real source for it in A22-0526-3 p.99.

OPCODE SPOT-CHECK: these findings contain no opcode table, so I spot-checked ten instruction rows implicated by the topic against the manual's own instruction descriptions in A22-0526-3 and 223-2588-2, and all ten match the findings' usage: Read a Card (M or L, %1x3, d=R, BAR=B+LB+1); Read a Card with x3=9 (data transferred, no stacker select, no feed, buffer retains image); Select Stacker and Feed (K or 4, d=0/1/2, BAR=Bp, word marks not affected); Punch a Card (M or L, %4x3, d=W); RCP (M, %T0, d=R, BAR=B+LB+1, WM undisturbed); RCPW (L, %T0, d=R, WM erased and entered); WCP (M, %T0, d=W, WM not indicated); Read/Write Tape with Word Marks (L, %Ux3 or %Bx3, d = R or W and $ or X, BAR=B+LB+1, X suppresses GM-WM termination); 1403 Printer (M or L, %20, d=W) and the %21 word-mark print form ('prints 1 for each position that contained a WM'); Card Punch stacker variants (%40 / %44 / %48, d=W). No 1401-vs-1410 opcode confusion found in the findings themselves - the finder consistently labelled which machine each fact belongs to. The confusion risk I did find is in the surrounding literature, and I added the two concrete traps (1401 LOAD KEY blanket 002-080 word-mark clear; 1401 greedy vs 1410 pairwise word-separator runs) as additions.

COULD NOT REACH / STILL OPEN: 223-2597 (1410/1401 Compatibility CE Instruction manual) - not read, so open question 5 stays open; open question 1 (an 80th card column that is a word separator with nothing following) is genuinely undocumented in everything I read, and I did not find any manual sentence either way; open question 3 I converted into a refutation above but its exact card code for the group mark, and whether an object-deck format can produce WS followed by a group mark, I did not verify.
